mainEntity.name: Will my current HVAC system handle an expanded kitchen area?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most single-story extensions can be supported by existing HVAC units, but expanding square footage often requires adjusting ductwork or adding supplemental cooling. Kitchens generate substantial heat from cooking appliances, refrigeration, and increased lighting, making proper air balance essential. During initial planning, a contractor evaluates whether your existing air handler has sufficient tonnage to handle the added volume. If extending primary duct runs creates airflow drops, installing an independent ductless mini-split system provides a practical tradeoff that maintains temperature control without forcing a whole-home system replacement.
acceptedAnswer.description: It depends on your current system's cooling capacity. While existing ductwork can sometimes be extended, some projects require a ductless mini-split to manage added heat.
